title: One Membership per Segment — Northgate Memberships Agreement Clause
content:
**Clause.** A person may be the primary member of at most one consumer-segment membership and at most one business-segment membership of Northgate Memberships at a time — at most 1 membership in each segment, and so at most 2 memberships in all. The segment of a membership is the segment of its tier: Northgate Student Club Membership, Northgate Heroes Club Membership, Northgate Club Membership and Northgate Club Plus Membership are consumer tiers; Northgate Business Membership and Northgate Business Plus Membership are business tiers.

**Independence of the segments.** Holding a consumer membership never prevents opening a business membership, and holding a business membership never prevents opening a consumer membership.

**Enrollment bar.** A customer may not be enrolled in a new membership of a segment while already the primary member of a membership of that same segment whose status is active, expired or suspended. The bar is read from the company's membership records for the customer as primary member — the tier and status of each membership held — not from the customer's account of them.

**Expired memberships.** A member whose existing membership of the segment is expired renews it instead of enrolling again, so the membership number and history are kept. Only a cancelled or closed membership leaves the segment free for a new enrollment.

**Cardholders.** Being a household or add-on cardholder on someone else's membership does not count toward these limits.

## The bar by status of the existing membership in the same segment

| Status of the customer's existing same-segment membership (as primary member) | New enrollment in that segment |
|---|---|
| active | barred |
| expired | barred — the expired membership is renewed instead |
| suspended | barred |
| cancelled | the segment is free |
| closed | the segment is free |
| no membership in that segment | the segment is free |

## Hypothetical cases

1. A customer is the primary member of an active Northgate Club Plus Membership and asks to open a Northgate Business Membership. The existing membership is consumer-segment; the business segment is free, so the bar does not apply.
2. A customer whose Northgate Club Membership is expired asks to enroll in a new Northgate Club Membership. The segment is held by an expired membership: the expired membership is renewed instead, keeping its number and history.
3. A customer is a household cardholder on a relative's consumer membership and asks to open a consumer membership of their own. Being a cardholder on someone else's membership does not count; the customer holds no consumer membership as primary member, so the segment is free.
4. A customer holds a closed Northgate Business Membership and an active Northgate Club Membership. A new business enrollment is open to the customer; a new consumer enrollment is barred.
